title: Where does an archetype's example content come from, and which settings must an author supply?
description: ST-DECL-UC01-R01 and R04 say each archetype supplies the smallest example content that checking accepts, and R05 says an empty scaffold names every setting the author must supply. Today the scaffolds of rpc-service and browser-service are refused: rpc-service needs the grpc-processes settings processes and proto_files, a proto file and a process factory package (factory/rpc.go) that imports the generated packages by the module path; browser-service needs a distinct api_prefix. The Archetype entity (ST-SUP-EN03) has no field that holds example content, and a component schema marks as required both settings the declaration must give and settings that only the running service gets (such as connection_string of postgres-adapter and issuer of jwt-auth), so checking cannot tell which settings an author must supply. Options: (a) add to the Archetype an example content field (files under the archetype folder and the settings to write into the declaration, with the module path as a placeholder), and mark in a component schema each setting the declaration must give, so that checking refuses its absence and init can name it; (b) keep the example content in Declaring's code, one case per archetype; (c) narrow R01, R04 and R05 to archetypes that can be empty, such as rest-crud. Recommendation: (a), since the UC01 notes say the archetype supplies its example content, and a registry change then needs no change to STEGO's code. Until then UC01-R01, R04-T01, R05 and the flow test stay not automated; rest-crud, which can be empty, already passes as written.

title: Which step of Record what a service was built from fulfills that apply writes the record inside the service's repo?
description: ST-GEN-UC01-R05 says that apply MUST write the record inside the service's repo, beside the code it generated. Only the step ST-GEN-UC01-FL-S02 (the service author commits the record with the generated code) fulfills it, and that step invokes no command, so no technical record can build the requirement, although ST-GEN-UC01-R05-T01 is automated and passes. Options: (a) ST-GEN-UC01-FL-S01, which invokes Apply a plan (ST-GEN-CMD01), also fulfills ST-GEN-UC01-R05, and S02 keeps it too; (b) S02 also invokes Apply a plan; (c) the requirement stays proved and not built. Recommendation: (a), since apply is what writes the record in the repo and the commit only shows it.

title: Is a denied get query answered 403 or 404?
description: ST-SUP-RC33-OC05 and its test T01 say that the handler answers a deny of a get query's permission with 403. The later decisions ST-SUP-RP11-LC06 and ST-SUP-RP11-LC17 say that a denied read is not found, the same as a missing row, and query.Serve answers it with 404; the runtime gives no error that Serve answers with 403. The generator decides the permission before the fill through the handle's read, so a deny and a missing row are both 404 and neither calls the fill (proved through the generated service in internal/generator/query/testdata/query_test.go). Options: (a) change OC05 and OC05-T01 to answer a deny with 404, the same as a missing row, as LC06 and LC17 do; (b) keep 403: the runtime adds an error for a deny before the fill that Serve answers with 403, which tells the caller that the row exists. Recommendation: (a), because a 403 tells a caller which IDs exist. OC05-T01 stays not automated until this is decided.

title: How does query.Serve answer a declared refusal with its status and code?
description: ST-SUP-RC33-OC07 says that the handler answers a declared refusal with its declared status and code, and any other error with 500 and the code internal, in the response, the audit row's error_code and the completion log. query.Serve (ST-SUP-RP11-LC17) answers every error it does not know with 500, and its problem response holds no code member; generated code cannot change the answer, because Serve writes it. The generator emits the typed refusal values and queries.Declared, which gives the status and code of a refusal of one query. Options: (a) the runtime adds to query.HTTP a function such as Refusal func(error) (status int, code string, ok bool), which the generated code sets to queries.Declared, and Serve writes the code in the problem response and gives it to the read audit row and the completion log; (b) the runtime defines its own refusal type that generated code makes. Recommendation: (a), because only the declaration varies. OC07 stays not built until this is decided.

title: Over which transport is a stream query served, and how does the generator know a query is a stream?
description: The query runtime has RunStream (ST-SUP-RP11-LC13) but no HTTP helper for a stream, and the declaration marks a query as a stream only by a gRPC method that is a server stream (ST-DECL-INV73), whose check is not built, so the compiler cannot tell the generator. The generator emits, for each query in gen.Context.QueryStreams, the stream slot type, a Bind function and a Stream function on query.RunStream for the transport; the service test carries the messages as JSON lines over HTTP itself. Options: (a) a stream is served over gRPC only: the compiler fills QueryStreams from the proto files when ST-DECL-INV73 is built, and the grpc-application component calls the generated Stream function; (b) the declaration gets a stream kind for HTTP and the runtime adds query.ServeStream (for example JSON lines), so the generated code passes only what varies; (c) both. Recommendation: (a), as the declaration states now; (b) only when an HTTP client needs a stream.

title: May a query fill import out/queries, the query slot's contract package?
description: ST-EXT-INV05 says that a fill imports only the package out/slots, which holds the contract of each slot. The query slot is a Go contract, not a protobuf message: its request, handle and fill types, repositories and refusals are in the generated package out/queries, which a query fill imports, and that package reaches the runtime library. ST-EXT-UC01-R03 says the slot's contract. Options: (a) INV05 names each slot's contract package: out/slots for a protobuf slot, out/queries for the query slot and the command generator's package for the command slot, and the import rule admits the packages of the runtime library that the contract reaches; (b) the capability generators emit their contracts into out/slots. Recommendation: (a), because the contract of the query slot needs the runtime library's types and out/slots is the compiler's. Until this is decided, stego test refuses evidence for a query fill (checkImports).
